before: attr_reader :steps creates a public steps method that reads @steps. It does not create a steps= writer. attr_accessor would create both methods.

Keep mutation behind a method such as add_step when callers should perform an operation instead of assigning arbitrary state. A reader returning a mutable object would still expose that object; it is not a deep read-only guarantee.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
class Goal
  attr_reader :steps
  def initialize
    @steps = 0
  end
  def add_step
    @steps += 1
  end
end
goal = Goal.new
goal.add_step
puts goal.steps
```
